figure_candidates.label: Figure 1
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 1. Peramine (1) is an insect feeding deterrent biosynthesized
from arginine and hydroxyproline by the two-module, nonribosomal
peptide synthetase PpzA, originally discovered in Epichloë species of
endophytic fungi. (A) PPZ gene cluster in Metarhizum majus, which
contains ppzA as a central component. (B) Summary of the reaction
carried out by PpzA.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 2
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 2. In vitro reactions with PpzD and L-proline were found to
yield trans-4-hydroxy-L-proline (2) and trans-3-hydroxy-L-proline (3)
via Fmoc derivatization followed by LCMS, selectively monitoring [M
+ H]+ = 354.1 m/z. (A) Reversed-phase and chiral chromatography
analyses of reaction products, compared with heat-inactivated enzyme
and analytical standards. (B) Summary of reactions performed by
PpzD.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 3
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 3. In vitro and in vivo reactions with PpzC and peramine
yielded compound 5 with m/z = 264.1455, corresponding to [M +
H]+ = C12H17N5O2. (A) Base peak chromatograms of the in vitro
reaction, yielding a small amount of 5, and the reaction with heat-
inactivated enzyme as a control. (B) Base peak chromatogram of in
vivo biosynthesis of 5 in Escherichia coli..

figure_candidates.label: Figure 4
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 4. PpzC reacts with peramine to yield 8-hydroxyperamine (5).
(A) Summary of the reaction carried out by PpzC. (B) 1H (600
MHz) and 13C (150 MHz) NMR data acquired in DMSO-d6, and key
NMR correlations observed in 5.
